mcqs.question: Which of the following best defines a random experiment in probability?

options.A: An experiment whose outcome is predetermined and known in advance.
options.B: An experiment that can be performed repeatedly under the same conditions, and whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty.
options.C: An experiment that always yields the same result each time it is performed.
options.D: An experiment that involves only deterministic processes.

mcqs.answer: An experiment that can be performed repeatedly under the same conditions, and whose outcome cannot be predicted with certainty.
mcqs.explanation: A random experiment is one that can be repeated under identical conditions, yet its individual outcome cannot be predicted in advance. Option B captures this definition. Option A describes a deterministic experiment, C is incorrect because outcomes vary, and D is unrelated.

mcqs.question: In the context of probability, an "outcome" refers to:

options.A: The set of all possible results of an experiment.
options.B: A single possible result of a random experiment.
options.C: A collection of several experiments performed together.
options.D: The probability of an event occurring.

mcqs.answer: A single possible result of a random experiment.
mcqs.explanation: An outcome is one specific result that may occur when a random experiment is performed. Option B states this precisely. Option A describes the sample space, C is not a definition of outcome, and D confuses outcome with probability.

mcqs.question: The sample space of a random experiment is:

options.A: The set of all elementary events only.
options.B: The set of all possible outcomes of the experiment.
options.C: The set of outcomes that are impossible.
options.D: The set of outcomes that have probability zero.

mcqs.answer: The set of all possible outcomes of the experiment.
mcqs.explanation: The sample space (denoted S) contains every outcome that can possibly occur when the experiment is carried out. Option B is correct. Option A is too restrictive, C and D describe impossible or null events, not the full sample space.

mcqs.question: An event in probability is:

options.B: Any subset of the sample space, including possibly a single outcome or multiple outcomes.
options.C: The complement of the sample space.

mcqs.answer: Any subset of the sample space, including possibly a single outcome or multiple outcomes.
mcqs.explanation: An event is defined as any collection (subset) of outcomes from the sample space. It may consist of one outcome (elementary) or many (compound). Option B states this. Option A limits events incorrectly, C describes a specific event (complement), and D confuses event with probability distribution.

mcqs.question: Consider tossing a fair coin twice. Let S be the sample space. Which of the following correctly identifies an elementary event and a compound event?

options.A: ‘Head on first toss’ is elementary; ‘Exactly one head in two tosses’ is compound.
options.B: ‘Exactly one head in two tosses’ is elementary; ‘Head on first toss’ is compound.

mcqs.answer: ‘Head on first toss’ is elementary; ‘Exactly one head in two tosses’ is compound.
mcqs.explanation: ‘Head on first toss’ corresponds to a single specific outcome (e.g., HH or HT) and is therefore elementary. ‘Exactly one head in two tosses’ includes two outcomes (HT, TH) and is a compound event. Option A captures this distinction. Options B, C, D misclassify the events.

mcqs.question: A student draws a card at random from a standard deck of 52 cards and notes its suit. Which description best matches this situation?

options.A: A deterministic experiment because the suit can be known beforehand.
options.B: A random experiment because the outcome (the suit) cannot be predicted with certainty before drawing.
options.C: A non-random experiment because the deck is fixed.
options.D: A random experiment only if the card is replaced after each draw.

mcqs.answer: A random experiment because the outcome (the suit) cannot be predicted with certainty before drawing.
mcqs.explanation: Drawing a card without looking is a random experiment: the specific suit is uncertain until the draw. Option B correctly states this. Option A is false because the suit is not known in advance. Option C misinterprets randomness, and D adds an unnecessary condition about replacement.

mcqs.question: Which statement about an outcome is FALSE?

options.A: An outcome is one possible result of a random experiment.
options.B: All outcomes together form the sample space.
options.C: An outcome can be a set of multiple results.
options.D: Each outcome is mutually exclusive with others.

mcqs.answer: An outcome can be a set of multiple results.
mcqs.explanation: An outcome is a single result, not a set. Therefore statement C is false. Statements A, B, and D are true: each outcome is a single result, the collection of all outcomes makes the sample space, and distinct outcomes cannot occur simultaneously in a single trial.

mcqs.question: If a die is rolled, which of the following correctly represents the sample space?
mcqs.explanation: When a standard six‑sided die is rolled, any of the numbers 1 through 6 can appear, so the sample space is {1,2,3,4,5,6}. Option C is correct. Option A omits 6, B includes an impossible 0, and D excludes odd numbers, all of which are incorrect representations of the full sample space.
